bc_second_ave.blurb: Second Ave is a small crag within the Smoke Bluffs, the cluster of granite cliffs on the edge of Squamish. Its 21 routes are short, around 15 m, and mostly traditional, with a few bolted lines and some that are often top-roped. Grades start at easy 5.4 and top out at a single 5.10, but most lines are 5.8 or easier, which makes it a friendly place for newer leaders to practise placing gear. Expect quick single-pitch outings rather than a full day of climbing, and it pairs easily with neighbouring crags in the bluffs.

bc_electric_avenue_east_face.blurb: This is the steeper side of Electric Avenue, a bolted crag in the Chek area of Cheakamus Canyon in the Sea to Sky corridor. All 21 routes are sport climbs. Grades begin with one 5.8, then centre on 5.10 and 5.11, with a handful at 5.12 and a single 5.13, so it suits climbers who are past the beginner stage. The wall looks west and catches afternoon sun, and a flat belay area along the base lets a party shift between sun and shade. Loose flakes near the ground are worth watching for.
bc_electric_avenue_east_face.approach: A short walk of about five minutes brings you to the flat belay area at the base, with the East Face on your right.

bc_red_tail_south.blurb: Red Tail South is a mid-sized wall in the Red Tail Group at Skaha Bluffs in the Okanagan, just south of Lower Red Tail. Its 21 climbs split between trad lines and bolted ones, and a couple run to two pitches. Grades cluster around 5.10, with a few 5.8s and 5.9s and a couple at 5.12, so there is a decent spread for a mixed party. The gneiss is not rated among the finest at Skaha, but the wall is convenient and sits among the most visited crags in the area, so expect company on busy days. The group as a whole gets sun for most of the day.

bc_brohm_dome.blurb: Brohm Dome is a sport-leaning crag just across Highway 99 from Brohm Lake, between Squamish and Whistler. Most of its 21 routes are bolted, with a handful of trad lines mixed in. The weight of the sport grades sits in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, with a couple of moderates around 5.9 and 5.10 and a few harder lines above them, so it is aimed at experienced sport climbers rather than beginners. The wall faces west and picks up filtered sun in the afternoon, and it works well as a half-day outing from Squamish.

bc_grand_wall_base_area.blurb: A west-facing granite section at the foot of the Stawamus Chief in Squamish, stretching north from the Dihedrals toward the University Wall. Its 20 routes are almost all trad, with a couple of bolted lines, and a few offer multi-pitch outings. Expect steep slab and face climbing broken up by cracks. Grades run from 5.8 through 5.11, with the bulk at 5.10 and 5.11, so it is a place for confident leaders rather than first-timers. The routes are shorter than those on the big wall above, and the surrounding forest gives more shade. A helmet is wise, since the cliff overhead is busy.

bc_lower_left_path.blurb: Lower Left Path is a bouldering area inside the Lower Left sector of the Stacks, a granite boulder field in the Fraser Valley close to Hope. The 20 problems here run from V0 to V6, with most falling between V1 and V5, so there is something for a range of abilities and a few lines for stronger climbers. Several of the sector's best-rated problems are found on this section. The wider Stacks is known for crack and offwidth climbing, with room for many more problems still to be developed.

bc_rimrocks.blurb: Rimrocks is a young sport crag in the North Okanagan, east of Vernon, where a north-facing cliff band looks over a long talus slope dotted with freestanding volcanic pillars. All 20 routes are bolted. Grades centre on 5.11, with plenty at 5.10 and 5.12, one 5.13 and a couple of easier warm-ups. The walls are long and overhanging, which rewards power endurance. Holds are plentiful, though some are worse than they appear from below. The rock is fresh and loose pieces can fall, so wear a helmet.
bc_rimrocks.parking_note: Drive east from Vernon on Highway 6 toward Lumby, then follow King Edward Forest Service Road, Brewer Road and Bolton Road to an unmarked pullout on the left.
bc_rimrocks.approach: Allow about ten minutes: a short stretch of old skid road to a big cairn, then a climbers' trail through the trees to the foot of the scree, then cairn-marked ground across the talus to the cliffs.
